0.long_answer: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a non-ionizing imaging technique used to form detailed images of the soft tissues of the body, including the heart and other internal organs. It is particularly useful in patients with conditions like situs inversus totalis, where the internal organs are completely reversed from their normal positions. Additionally, MRI’s ability to provide high-contrast images without the use of ionizing radiation makes it an attractive option for imaging delicate specimens such as mummies, whose preservation can be compromised by other imaging methods that utilize radiation.
